👤 Lama (12.9K) 🗓7h 👁️12.5K
Let’s talk about my biggest onchain conviction play. $Crawl

@crawlnetwork is one of those projects where I think people are looking at the first product & missing the actual company being built.

The obvious thing is “crypto LLM.” The bigger thesis is a model that becomes the intelligence layer for an entire industry, with the industry itself economically incentivized to build its training data.

Think about what that means. Crypto already produces an absurd amount of information, but it is scattered across chains, contracts, docs, GitHub, governance, funding rounds, markets, research and social data. Today you pay different companies to organize pieces of it, then manually connect the pieces. Nansen can charge up to $1,800/month, Glassnode up to $999, Chainalysis sells six-figure contracts, and the broader alternative-data market is already measured in billions.

An industry-specific LLM changes the product entirely. Instead of another terminal that shows you data, you have a model... Show more

Charity has always had a funding problem.

There are millions of people willing to help, but the systems connecting money to causes can be slow, fragmented, and difficult to track.

Crypto introduced something different: programmable money, global settlement, and transparent public transactions.

PlaguePad is exploring what happens when those properties are applied to charitable funding.

IRL3 has a compelling first-mover opportunity at the intersection of NFTs, 3D graphics and real-world assets. As demand for immersive digital experiences, gaming and digital collectibles evolves, IRL3 is exploring a new primitive: turning physical possessions into identifiable, tradable 3D assets onchain.

What makes this interesting is the potential to give everyday objects a second life in digital economies, extending NFTs beyond purely digital collectibles. If IRL3 can establish reliable object verification, scalable 3D generation and a liquid marketplace, it could become an early infrastructure layer connecting physical reality to digital ownership, with applications across gaming, commerce and virtual worlds.

👤 Tencent AI (24.5K) 🗓3h 👁️24.7K
We open sourced Octop, a multi-user AI workspace for yourself, your family and your team.

Everyone gets their own login and can create multiple agents, each with its own workspace. Nothing you say or save shows up in another account. Almost everything can be swapped: models, storage, memory, plugins. Each agent comes with a browser, a terminal and a remote desktop.

You can hand off work to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, CodeBuddy and other coding agents you already use. It also lives in your group chats on Telegram and Discord.

It runs on your own machine, and one command is all it takes: octop run.

The full picture is in the repo: github.com/TencentCloud/O….
